To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The global economic crisis caused a severe output collapse in the developing world.
the 2009 output collapse was more severe in countries that were more integrated to the world economy, had low reserves or high external debt in 2007, and that were relatively rich in 2007.
developing countries that were highly dependent on exports and had relatively low reserves were more deeply affected in the crisis years.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the global financial crisis on developing countries and the factors that have made them more vulnerable to external shocks.
the sources of vulnerability of the developing countries to the global economic crisis.
two issues: 1) the impact of the global crisis on developing countries; and 2) the sources of vulnerability to the crisis in the developing countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the more export dependent an economy is, the more its GDP growth rate will be negatively affected by the crisis, and this is the main source of vulnerability.
the more dependent on foreign capital, the less the negative impact of the global economic crisis on the developing economies.
developing countries with high dependence on exports, high short-term debts, and low reserves were more vulnerable to the global economic crisis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the crisis has affected the developing countries mainly through trade, and the impact has been stronger in those countries that are heavily dependent on exports, have low reserves and/or have high short-term debt.

the more a middle income developing country depends on exports and the more it has low foreign reserves and high short-term debt the more its output is expected to fall during an external economic shock such as the 2007-08 crisis.
, in the middle-income developing economies, export dependence and low reserves were the main sources of vulnerability during the crisis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while the developing countries have a lot of room to grow and catch up with the developed countries, their growth potential can be easily undermined by external shocks, such as the global economic crisis.
developing countries are more vulnerable to the global economic crisis when they are more integrated to the world economy.
the developing countries are vulnerable in terms of output to the global economic crises, but this vulnerability is not a function of their integration to the world economy, as it is often assumed.
